Michaela (CS): heads up — prepping AstraMed QBR next Tue, need a quick pulse on onboarding accounts that are burning over budget. Dashboard: https://redwood.app/d/astramed/costs ?view=token-burn
Michaela (CS): topline: 3 prod routes >150% baseline, overall token burn up 42% month-over-month, customer is on a mid-tier committed plan. need: 1) token-by-route breakdown 2) onboarding blockers that correlate to spikes 3) recommended quick wins for next-week enablement
Ben (Ops): saw the alert this morning. budget alert triggered at 78% of committed on 03/14. linked the alert: https://redwood.app/alerts/AM-4321
Ben (Ops): quick query you can run if you need a CSV:
```
SELECT route, sum(tokens) AS tokens, avg(latency_ms) AS avg_latency
FROM redwood_logs
WHERE customer_id='astramed' AND ts >= '2025-12-01'
GROUP BY route
ORDER BY tokens DESC;
```
Omar (AE): adding context — AstraMed just expanded to three new clinical-workflow routes in Jan. They enabled verbose debugging in one route (dev-engine) which might explain spike. Also their renewal touchpoint is in 10 days.
Evelyn (Solutions): for the QBR deck: we should propose a 2-step enablement: 1) short prompt template update + guardrails, 2) KV-cache strategy to avoid re-tokenizing static prefixes. I can draft a one-pager.
Michaela (CS): @Evelyn yes please. also Ben can you surface any onboarding tickets tied to those routes? want to see if errors coincide with token spikes.
Ben (Ops): on it. pulling tickets now — looks like 6 tickets referencing `dev-engine` in last 30 days, 2 are high-priority. linking shortlist to the QBR folder: https://redwood.app/spaces/astramed/qbr/docs
